name: file_type
description: Say what a file is from its first bytes, and whether that agrees with its extension, for a file or a directory walked in sorted order. Identifies with a table of forensic signatures (PE, ELF, Mach-O universal vs Java class by their own fields, archives, registry hives, event logs, prefetch at offset 4 and compressed MAM, shortcuts, AD1 and E01, memory captures) and, for what the table does not know, the installed `file` (libmagic) when present. An identification is a reading of the first bytes, not a validation. A type nothing knows is unrecognised and its extension_matches is null, neither match nor mismatch. Hashes every regular file it opens (SHA-256; a file the time budget ends in has no digest, and its entry says how far it got); plain text is consistent with any extension that is not a binary format's; a directory that cannot be listed is an error entry; symbolic links and non-regular files are listed, never opened or followed. examined counts files actually opened; the first bytes are returned only with head_hex: true; every result is kept in all_results when the inline page (limit, mismatch_only) is not the whole, and unreadable files are reported as errors whatever mismatch_only says. earlier_answers says how many other files answer the same question.

path.description: A file, or a directory to walk

mismatch_only.description: Show inline only files whose bytes disagree with their extension (errors and the complete result are still reported)

limit.description: Maximum files shown inline (default 500, at most 5000); every file looked at is in all_results when there are more

head_hex.description: Also return each file's first 16 bytes in hex (default false): the head of a key file or a credential store is the secret, so it is opt-in
